images.title: What is left on the tray
images.purpose: Show the whole chikki as 4 fourths, with 3 fourths eaten, so 1 fourth is left.
images.composition: One square tray in the centre with wide margins, holding the chikki cut into a 2 by 2 block, and one subtraction line below the tray.
images.exact_structure: One plain square tray outline in grey #6B7280. On it, one square chikki cut by one vertical and one horizontal line into 4 equal square pieces in 2 rows of 2. Three pieces drawn as empty dashed grey outlines to show they are eaten; the bottom right piece filled teal #0072B2 with a thin reddish purple #CC79A7 outline, the piece left. Centred below the tray: one subtraction line. Exactly 1 tray, 4 equal pieces, 3 eaten outlines, 1 teal piece.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
chikki pieces that are not equal, or fewer than 4 pieces drawn in all
images.takeaway: Write the whole as 4/4, then take away the fourths eaten.
images.description: A square chikki on a tray cut into 4 equal pieces: 3 dashed outlines show the 3/4 eaten and 1 teal piece shows the 1/4 left, since 4/4 − 3/4 = 1/4.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count all 4 pieces, eaten and left, and say what part of the whole chikki is left.

image_decisions.why: Keeping the eaten pieces as outlines shows the whole is still 4 fourths, which is the key point.
